title: BC/DR nesting and control-like scope labels obscure the teaching relationship
location: domain-2.md:181–195; diagram-generator.js:1501–1593; reading.css diagram scope/mobile scope rules
issue: The diagram uses an outer card, BC enclosure, DR enclosure, badges, five pill-shaped labels and a further examples panel. On phone the containment consumes most of the available 328 px reading width. Scope nouns look like controls although they have no interaction. Examples compete with category framing.
rootCause: Repeated nested framing and decorative badge/pill styling perform several visual jobs without a clear priority.
recommendation: Pilot one simple BC scope boundary with a clearly labelled technology-recovery contribution and examples as ordinary adjacent text. Show People, Processes, Facilities, Suppliers and Technology as non-interactive scope labels. Preserve every example and the existing correct DR translation. Suggested relationship caption: “DR supports business continuity through technology and system recovery / DR สนับสนุนความต่อเนื่องทางธุรกิจด้วยการกู้คืนเทคโนโลยีและระบบ”.
qualification: Containment is an acceptable introductory scope model, not a newly confirmed academic error or a universal set-theory claim about all DR practices. Button-like appearance is an affordance assessment, not a claim that users clicked these controls in usability testing.
prior: Academic D2-06 translation is already corrected; this is a separate presentation issue.
confidence: High for structure; medium for perceived affordance

title: Measurement aid retains a numbered hierarchy despite corrected non-mandatory prose
issue: Desktop puts 06 Report at the top, 04/05 in the next row, 02/03 below and 01 Metric at the bottom, linked by a dashed vertical spine. Mobile presents 06 down to 01. The region name still says “6-Part Framework”. Numbering, reading order and architecture framing imply more order/officialness than the correct explanatory paragraph warrants.
rootCause: A local memory aid is encoded as a tiered numbered architecture rather than a relationship between kinds of measures and communication forms.
recommendation: Group by function: “Measurement and indicators / การวัดและตัวชี้วัด” (Metric, with purpose-selected KPI and KRI) and “Presentation and communication / การนำเสนอและสื่อสาร” (Dashboard, Scorecard, Report). Remove step ordinals and workflow connectors unless attached to an explicitly optional worked example. Label it as a local study aid in visible and accessible text. Preserve all six definitions and examples.
qualification: Batch A already corrected Metric as including KPI/KRI, and current Thai prose expressly rejects a mandatory sequence. Do not re-open that academic correction or claim the current prose explicitly attributes six steps to ISC2. The outline lists topics, not this architecture; provenance as AI-generated is not established.
prior: Residual visual issue related to D2-04, not a recurrence of its corrected raw-data-only definition.

title: English terminology fragments in compressed comparison tables
location: domain-2.md:441–448; reading.css:2828–2853; markdown-parser.js table renderer:459–493; additional occurrences in coverage matrix
issue: At 1366 px, the memory-aid table is 915 px wide but its first column is only 91 px: Dashboard and Scorecard break mid-word. At 390 px, four columns squeeze into 328 px; the first is about 55 px. At 320 px they squeeze into 258 px, with a roughly 50 px first column. Even Metric/KPI and ordinary trigger phrases fragment. The sweep finds unhyphenated mid-word breaks in 15 subsection ranges across all four domains.
rootCause: Generic table auto sizing plus width:100% and word-break/overflow-wrap:break-word permits columns to shrink below technical-term needs. Most affected tables do not adopt the GRC table’s contained minimum-width behavior.
recommendation: Pilot meaningful term/description/example column roles, preserve whole English words and mixed-language phrase boundaries, allocate sufficient keyword width, and use a labelled contained scrolling comparison where needed. Retain row/column relationships and current font sizes. Consider a narrow definition presentation only if it preserves comparison tasks; do not universally convert tables to cards.
qualification: Severity P1 describes severe phone fragmentation in this root-cause family; desktop two-line wrapping is P2 in isolation. Normal wrapping at spaces or intentional hyphens is excluded from the affected-range count. Horizontal scrolling itself is not a defect and WCAG permits necessary two-dimensional tables.
prior: Related RN-I-014; the specific Dashboard/Scorecard and broader 15-range mapping are fresh current evidence.

title: Scaled SVG instructional text is too small; JML is the mandatory exemplar
issue: JML uses an 840×220 viewBox. At 1366 px the wrapper has 867 px but the SVG caps at 760×199 px; minimum instructional text is 9.95 px. At 1024 px it renders at 525×137.5 px, with 6.88 px minimum text. All 24 diagram payloads in 23 subsection ranges have small labels at that width: D1 minimum 6.72, D2/D3 6.56, D4 5.62 px. Continuous Governance is a short, visually weak strip.
rootCause: Authored 10–12 px SVG labels are scaled by broad fixed viewBoxes, maximum-width caps and a viewport-only 768 px representation breakpoint. The desktop rail reduces the actual component width well before that breakpoint.
recommendation: Pilot JML and a dense D4 diagram with a component-width-driven representation and a legibility budget for actual transformed instructional text. Use available width/height, enlarge/wrap labels and reduce unused space. Keep governance legible and explicit. Allow diagrams with different information density to adapt differently. Validate full-width and sidebar-open/collapsed cases without changing Phase 2 navigation.
qualification: Phone/tablet ≤768 px use a separate HTML representation; do not report the hidden desktop SVG as tiny visible phone text. A readable font-size budget is a product acceptance target, not a fabricated WCAG minimum-font-size rule. Contrast is separately counted under ACC-001.
prior: RN-I-001 remains confirmed; JML is an occurrence, not a second global defect.

title: Concept-group labels remain ordinary paragraphs with weak local rhythm
origin: User-reported; similar source patterns newly mapped
location: domain-4.md:9–27,96–149,178–208,243–313; reading.css:591–597,660–694; additional ranges in coverage matrix
issue: Network Scope, Collision & Broadcast Domains and architectural reach are plain paragraph labels, not navigable subheadings. They inherit normal 15.5 px / 27.9 px prose with 0 px top and 16 px bottom margins. The following list gets negative top spacing from p+ul. Three different classifications read as a continuous list/paragraph stream. Similar group transitions occur in address planning, wireless, recovery sites and IAM tools.
rootCause: Source encodes meaningful conceptual transitions as colon-ended paragraphs or bold list text; generic proximity rules cannot distinguish a group title from an ordinary list introduction.
recommendation: Promote meaningful concept-group labels to semantic h4 subheadings, or a definition-group structure where that is more appropriate. Keep definition, explanation and example together. Pilot content-sensitive group spacing on Network Fundamentals and DRP sites; preserve LAN/WAN/WLAN/PAN/VPN and every explanation. Avoid a global li-margin increase.
qualification: The content is not wrong because it is long. Some colon-ended introductory sentences correctly remain paragraphs. The ten mapped ranges are reviewed candidate occurrences of this structure problem, not a rule that every colon becomes a heading.
prior: Related RN-I-013/014 and Batch B presentation deferrals.

title: OSI layer titles are ordered-list labels rather than semantic subsections
location: domain-4.md:29–77; source starts seven numbered layer groups at line 40
issue: The DOM correctly nests bullet details under seven ol items, but exposes “1. Layer 7” through “7. Layer 1”. Those ordinal markers compete with actual layer numbers. None of the seven layer names is a heading, despite each introducing multiple responsibilities, protocol/technology examples and PDU details.
rootCause: Semantic teaching sections are authored as a numbered outer list. This is a source-structure choice; the current list parser is not shown to have flattened these nested details.
recommendation: Promote Layer 7 through Layer 1 to h4 headings with their existing English/Thai names. Group the existing responsibility, technology/protocol, example and PDU detail under each. qualification: Layer numbering and the current mnemonic direction are already accurate. Do not hide list markers with CSS, reverse the mnemonic, or treat all numbered concept collections as false workflows.

title: JML connectors imply a compulsory Mover stage
origin: Newly discovered visual-semantic distinction within user-reported JML target
location: domain-3.md:9–38; diagram-generator.js:1877–1982 desktop arrows and mobile down-arrows
issue: 01 Joiner → 02 Mover → 03 Leaver is shown as a single path in both representations. A learner may infer every account must pass through a role-change event before offboarding, or that Mover happens only once.
rootCause: A possible employee journey is drawn as an unconditional lifecycle state machine without optional/repeated transitions.
recommendation: Show join/provision, an active-access period with ongoing review, optional repeated role-change/re-evaluation, and offboarding reachable without a role change. Keep Continuous Governance spanning relevant account activity. Alternatively label the current path explicitly as one possible example and show the direct Joiner-to-Leaver alternative.
qualification: This confirms a visual ambiguity, not a claim that the prose literally forbids direct departure. The official outline 3.1 lists provisioning/review/deprovisioning activities; it does not prescribe the pictured J→M→L sequence.

title: Cloud provider legend clips inside its own SVG
issue: The CSP Responsibility label extends beyond the right SVG edge while SVG overflow is hidden. Document width remains contained, so a page-overflow-only check misses the truncation. The legend identifies responsibility and is instructional content.
rootCause: A long bilingual label has insufficient viewBox space; width scaling does not make its logical bounds fit.
recommendation: Wrap or reposition the full legend, or make it adjacent semantic HTML. Retain the academically corrected distinction between customer governance/configuration and provider-operated controls. Check text bounds against the SVG viewport after fonts settle.
qualification: No new shared-responsibility academic error is inferred. The mobile HTML alternative is a different representation and not automatically affected by this SVG clipping.

title: GRC protected keyword exceeds its padded final cell
issue: At 1024/390 px, the special table is 780 px wide and its wrapper has 791 px scroll width. “Enterprise IT Governance” extends 11.08 px beyond the final cell’s right border in both themes. Preserving nowrap avoids fragments but does not guarantee padded cell fit.
rootCause: The fixed percentage/minimum-width special case does not account for the actual keyword width plus horizontal padding. Recognition also depends on exact table-header content.
recommendation: Treat this separately from generic table compression: size the keyword column for measured text plus padding, or allow wrapping at word boundaries. Preserve readable body type, explicit column headers and contained scrolling. Replace content-sniffing only if a narrowly reviewed semantic hook is needed.
qualification: Native Chrome scrolling worked: focus on the scroll wrapper plus ArrowRight moved it 40 px in both themes. Do not call the wrapper keyboard-inaccessible or all horizontal scrolling broken. The measured problem is cell fit, not merely the existence of overflow.

title: Instructional labels have insufficient contrast in specific settled themes
origin: Previously identified; exact current occurrences measured
location: reading.css .diag-text-sub and diagram support tokens; diagram-generator.js iamLifecycle governance strip/badges; scenario answer label reading.css:2767
issue: JML governance text is 2.89:1 on white in Light and 3.87:1 on the dark panel in Dark. The Dark Joiner badge is 3.48:1 white-on-blue; the Light badge is 5.17:1 and should not be called a failure. Scenario answer labels are 11.5 px green with 2.54:1 on white; the same label is 7.30:1 in Dark. Other SVG muted sublabels have similar theme-specific failures.
rootCause: Support-text and colored-label tokens are reused for small instructional text; theme palettes and real painted backgrounds are not consistently paired for normal-text contrast.
recommendation: Adjust only the relevant foreground/background token pairs and badge text choices; target ≥4.5:1 for normal instructional text. Keep labels so color is not the sole meaning carrier. Recheck effective text sizes, composited backgrounds and both themes after transitions settle.
qualification: Ratios are computed using actual rendered fills; SVG backgrounds are inferred from the last preceding containing rect and manually checked on the named samples. Do not certify every complex overlapping/gradient paint from that heuristic. No blanket color-only failure is asserted.

title: Thai instructional passages inherit the English page language
location: index.html document lang=en; Reading article/source passages; browser-results.json language/langParts
issue: All 94 ranges inherit the English document language; no language-of-parts attributes were found in these ranges. Long Thai explanatory passages therefore lack a programmatically determined Thai language.
rootCause: The bilingual corpus is rendered as unannotated mixed-language content under a monolingual page declaration.
recommendation: Plan a Reading-local Thai language scope with appropriate explicit English passage annotations where meaningful. Apply consistently to authored source, scenarios and generated instructional components, without changing the global app language or text content.
qualification: WCAG language-of-parts has exceptions for technical terms, proper names and vernacular words. It does not require annotating every borrowed English cybersecurity word. Native screen-reader voice switching was not manually tested; the missing language metadata itself is confirmed.
